answer: Locks are written down in ocean, expire in mirror, and horizon lists each expiry. The admission bond is time locked for 12 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. A hostile operator running 186 aliases therefore needs 154 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. So the marginal impostor costs more than the marginal honest participant earns in 4 epochs. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
